instructions: Rinse the 1 1/2 cups rice in a sieve until the water runs mostly clear. Put it in a saucepan with 2 1/4 cups water and 1/2 tsp of the salt and bring it to a boil over high.
Turn the heat to low, cover the pan and cook for 15 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on for 10 minutes. No peeking.
Meanwhile, slice each chicken breast in half horizontally so you have thin cutlets of even thickness. Pat them dry.

Mix the 2 tsp cumin, 2 tsp paprika, 1 tsp onion powder, 1 tsp oregano, the 1/4 tsp pepper and 1 tsp of the salt in a small bowl. Rub 1 tbsp of the oil over the chicken, then sprinkle the spice mix over both sides.
Dice the onion and the red pepper and mince the 2 garlic cloves. Drain the corn.

Heat a large skillet over medium high with no oil. Add the corn and leave it for 2 minutes, then stir and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until some kernels are browned. Transfer it into a bowl and wipe out the skillet.

Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in the skillet over high. Lay in the chicken and cook for 2 minutes, until the underside is golden. Flip it and cook the other side for 1 1/2 to 2 minutes. You're cooking it to 160°F in the thickest part, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Cut into the thickest piece: it's done when there's no pink left. Move it to a board and let it rest for 3 minutes.

Turn the heat to medium and add the last 1 tbsp oil. Add the onion and pepper and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring now and then, until the onion is soft. Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds, until you can smell it.

Chop the chicken into bite size pieces. Add it to the skillet with the can of refried beans, 1/4 cup water and the remaining pinch of salt. Stir and cook for 2 minutes, until it's thick and glossy and heated through.
Chop a large handful of the cilantro. Halve, pit and slice the avocado.
Taste the chicken and beans. If they're flat, add a pinch more salt.
Fluff the rice with a fork and divide it among 4 bowls. Top with the chicken and beans, the corn, the 1 1/2 cups cheese, the avocado, the 1/2 cup sour cream, 1 cup of the salsa and the cilantro.
Serve with the hot sauce on the side.
To pack them for lunch, divide the rice, the chicken and beans, the corn and the cheese into containers. Pack the avocado, sour cream and salsa separately and add them when you eat.
method_notes: No bowl version read had 20 or more ratings, so this one leads with RecipeTin Eats (the trusted cook for Mexican) and its Chicken Burrito filling, served in a bowl instead of a tortilla. RecipeTin Eats rubs thin chicken breast cutlets in a cumin, paprika, oregano and onion powder mix, sears them hard, then cooks onion, garlic and red pepper in the same pan and stirs the chopped chicken through refried beans with a splash of water, serving it with rice, corn, cheese and cilantro. Cooking Classy marinates thighs in lime and chili powder and chars the corn in the skillet, and Kristine's Kitchen builds the bowl over cilantro lime rice and romaine with pico de gallo. This one keeps RecipeTin's filling, leaves out the cayenne so it stays mild, chars the corn and puts hot sauce on the side.
